s.t: A miller lived with his three sons.
s.fr: Un meunier vivait avec ses trois fils.

s.t: He owned a mill, a donkey, and a cat.
s.fr: Il possédait un moulin, un âne, et un chat.

paras.summary: A miller lives with his three sons and owns a mill, a donkey, and a cat, with little else.

s.t: One day, the old miller died.
s.fr: Un jour, le vieux meunier mourut.

s.t: His mill, his donkey, and his cat went to his sons.
s.fr: Son moulin, son âne, et son chat allèrent à ses fils.

s.t: The oldest son got the mill.
s.fr: Le fils aîné reçut le moulin.

s.t: The second son got the donkey.
s.fr: Le deuxième fils reçut l’âne.

s.t: The youngest son got only the cat.
s.fr: Le fils cadet reçut seulement le chat.

paras.summary: One day the old miller dies, so his mill goes to the oldest son, his donkey to the second son, and his cat to the youngest.

s.t: The youngest son was not happy with his gift.
s.fr: Le fils cadet n’était pas content de son cadeau.

s.t: "My brothers can grind grain and ride to town," he said.
s.fr: « Mes frères peuvent moudre le grain et aller à cheval en ville, » dit-il.

s.t: "I can only eat this cat," he said to the cat.
s.fr: « Je ne peux que manger ce chat, » dit-il au chat.

s.t: "After that, I will have nothing at all," he said.
s.fr: « Après cela, je n’aurai rien du tout, » dit-il.

s.t: The cat sat near him and listened to every word.
s.fr: Le chat s’assit près de lui et écouta chaque mot.

paras.summary: The youngest son is not happy with his gift and says his brothers can work or travel while he can only eat the cat and then have nothing at all, but the cat sits near him and listens to every word.

s.t: The cat looked up at the youngest son.
s.fr: Le chat leva les yeux vers le fils le plus jeune.

s.t: "Do not eat me," the cat said.
s.fr: « Ne me mange pas, » dit-il le chat.

s.t: The son was surprised the cat could talk.
s.fr: Le fils fut surpris que le chat puisse parler.

s.t: "I can help you," said the cat.
s.fr: « Je peux vous aider, » dit le chat.

s.t: "Bring me a bag and a pair of boots."
s.fr: « Apportez-moi un sac et une paire de bottes. »

s.t: His brothers had laughed at his gift.
s.fr: Ses frères avaient ri de son cadeau.

s.t: The son had nothing to lose.
s.fr: Le fils n’avait rien à perdre.

paras.summary: The cat surprises the youngest son by talking and promises to help him, asking for a bag and a pair of boots; his brothers have already laughed at his gift, so with nothing to lose, the son agrees and brings them to the cat.

s.t: He brought the bag and boots to the cat.
s.fr: Il apporta le sac et les bottes au chat.

s.t: The cat put the boots on his feet.
s.fr: Le chat mit les bottes à ses pieds.

s.t: The cat put the bag over his shoulder.
s.fr: Le chat mit le sac sur son épaule.

s.t: "I will make you rich," the cat said.
s.fr: « Je vous ferai riche, » dit-il le chat.

s.t: The son did not believe the cat.
s.fr: Le fils ne crut pas le chat.

s.t: But he had no better plan.
s.fr: Mais il n’avait pas de meilleur plan.

paras.summary: The cat puts on the boots and slings the bag over his shoulder, looking ready for a journey and promising to make the son rich, though the son does not believe him and simply has no better plan.

s.t: A field lay near the mill.
s.fr: Un champ se trouvait près du moulin.

s.t: The cat went there with his open bag.
s.fr: Le chat y alla avec son sac ouvert.

s.t: He put some grain inside the bag.
s.fr: Il mit du grain à l’intérieur du sac.

s.t: A young rabbit went into the bag to eat.
s.fr: Un jeune lapin entra dans le sac pour manger.

s.t: The cat closed the bag.
s.fr: Le chat ferma le sac.

s.t: Soon he brought the bag to the king's palace.
s.fr: Bientôt il apporta le sac au palais du roi.

paras.summary: A field lies near the mill, and the cat goes there with his open bag, putting grain inside it until a young rabbit goes into the bag to eat, so the cat closes the bag and soon brings it to the king's palace, his boots helping him on the journey.

s.t: The cat gave the rabbit to the king.
s.fr: Le chat donna le lapin au roi.

s.t: "A gift from the Marquis of Carabas," said the cat.
s.fr: « Un cadeau du Marquis de Carabas, » dit le chat.

s.t: The king was happy with the gift.
s.fr: Le roi était content du cadeau.

s.t: "Thank the Marquis for me," the king said.
s.fr: « Remerciez le Marquis pour moi », dit le roi.

s.t: Soon the cat went home.
s.fr: Bientôt le chat rentra chez lui.

s.t: The son knew nothing of this gift.
s.fr: Le fils ne savait rien de ce cadeau.

paras.summary: The cat gives the rabbit to the king as a gift from the Marquis of Carabas, and the happy king asks the cat to thank the Marquis, so the cat goes home, where the son knows nothing of the gift and only the cat knows of his clever plan.

s.t: Weeks went by, and the cat caught more gifts.
s.fr: Des semaines passèrent, et le chat attrapa d’autres cadeaux.

s.t: He caught partridges in the fields near the mill.
s.fr: Il attrapa des perdrix dans les champs près du moulin.

s.t: He brought every gift to the king's palace.
s.fr: Il apporta chaque cadeau au palais du roi.

s.t: The king always thanked the cat.
s.fr: Le roi remerciait toujours le chat.

s.t: The king wanted to meet the Marquis.
s.fr: Le roi voulait rencontrer le Marquis.

paras.summary: Weeks go by, and the cat keeps catching gifts, mostly partridges from the fields near the mill, always bringing every one to the king's palace in the name of the Marquis of Carabas; the king always thanks the cat and wants to meet the Marquis.

s.t: But the cat still had a secret plan.
s.fr: Mais le chat avait encore un plan secret.

s.t: This went on for many weeks.
s.fr: Cela continua pendant plusieurs semaines.

s.t: The son had nothing but the cat.
s.fr: Le fils n’avait que le chat.

s.t: The cat's plan would make him rich.
s.fr: Le plan du chat le rendrait riche.

s.t: The cat said nothing more.
s.fr: Le chat ne dit rien de plus.

paras.summary: But the cat still has a secret plan and looks happy with it, and this goes on for many weeks, with the son still having nothing but the cat, whose plan would one day make him rich, though the cat says nothing more.

s.t: One day, the cat heard news.
s.fr: Un jour, le chat entendit des nouvelles.

s.t: The king would ride by the river soon.
s.fr: Le roi passerait bientôt à cheval près de la rivière.

s.t: The king's young daughter was a princess.
s.fr: La jeune fille du roi était une princesse.

s.t: The princess would ride with the king.
s.fr: La princesse chevaucherait avec le roi.

s.t: The cat had a plan for the son.
s.fr: Le chat avait un plan pour le fils.

paras.summary: One day the cat hears news that the king will soon ride by the river with his young daughter, a princess, so the cat makes a plan for the son.

s.t: The cat wanted the son to look rich.
s.fr: Le chat voulait que le fils paraisse riche.

s.t: "Go swim in the river tomorrow," the cat said.
s.fr: « Va nager dans la rivière demain », dit-il le chat.

s.t: Grass was near the river there.
s.fr: De l’herbe poussait près de la rivière là.

paras.summary: The son still lives at the mill, and the cat wants him to look rich, telling him to go swim in the river tomorrow, where grass is near the river.

s.t: The son said nothing.
s.fr: Le fils ne dit rien.

s.t: He believed the cat now.
s.fr: Il croyait le chat maintenant.

s.t: He had seen many of the cat's gifts.
s.fr: Il avait vu beaucoup de cadeaux du chat.

s.t: Soon the Marquis of Carabas would meet the king.
s.fr: Bientôt le Marquis de Carabas allait rencontrer le roi.

s.t: The son went to the river the next day.
s.fr: Le fils alla à la rivière le lendemain.

paras.summary: The son says nothing, and he believes the cat now, having seen so many of his gifts; soon the Marquis of Carabas would meet the king, but only the cat knows this secret, so the son goes to the river the next day.

s.t: The son left his clothes on the grass.
s.fr: Le fils laissa ses vêtements sur l’herbe.

s.t: He swam in the river.
s.fr: Il nagea dans la rivière.

s.t: The cat got the clothes and hid them in some grass.
s.fr: Le chat prit les vêtements et les cacha dans de l’herbe.

s.t: Soon the king's coach was near the river.
s.fr: Bientôt le carrosse du roi était près de la rivière.

s.t: The young princess was with the king.
s.fr: La jeune princesse était avec le roi.

paras.summary: The son leaves his clothes on the grass and swims in the river, and the cat gets the clothes and hides them in some grass, just as the king's coach draws near the river with the young princess at his side.

s.t: The cat ran to the coach.
s.fr: Le chat courut vers le carrosse.

s.t: "My master's clothes are stolen!" the cat cried.
s.fr: « Les vêtements de mon maître sont volés ! » dit le chat.

s.t: The king still remembered the cat's many gifts.
s.fr: Le roi se souvenait encore des nombreux cadeaux du chat.

s.t: "This cat belongs to the Marquis of Carabas," the king said.
s.fr: « Ce chat appartient au Marquis de Carabas, » dit le roi.

paras.summary: The cat runs to the coach and cries that his master's clothes are stolen, and the king, remembering the cat's many gifts, says this cat belongs to the Marquis of Carabas and wants to help him.

s.t: The king wanted to help the Marquis.
s.fr: Le roi voulait aider le Marquis.

s.t: "Bring fine clothes for the Marquis," the king told his men.
s.fr: « Apportez de beaux vêtements pour le Marquis, » dit le roi à ses hommes.

s.t: The king's men brought the fine clothes to the river.
s.fr: Les hommes du roi apportèrent les beaux vêtements à la rivière.

s.t: The son put on the fine clothes.
s.fr: Le fils mit les beaux vêtements.

s.t: He looked like a rich marquis.
s.fr: Il ressemblait à un riche marquis.

paras.summary: "Bring fine clothes for the Marquis," the king tells his men, and they bring the fine clothes to the river, where the son puts them on and looks like a rich marquis, now knowing this was the cat's clever plan.

s.t: The princess looked at the young man.
s.fr: La princesse regarda le jeune homme.

s.t: She had fine clothes of her own.
s.fr: Elle avait ses propres beaux vêtements.

s.t: She liked him.
s.fr: Elle l’aimait.

paras.summary: The princess looks at the young man; she has fine clothes of her own and likes him.

s.t: "Come ride with us," the king said.
s.fr: « Venez voyager avec nous, » dit le roi.

s.t: The young man got into the coach.
s.fr: Le jeune homme monta dans le carrosse.

s.t: He thanked the king.
s.fr: Il remercia le roi.

s.t: He sat next to the princess.
s.fr: Il s’assit à côté de la princesse.

s.t: The king was happy with the young Marquis.
s.fr: Le roi était content du jeune Marquis.

paras.summary: "Come ride with us," the king says, so the young man gets into the coach, thanks the king, and sits next to the princess, with the king happy with the young Marquis.

s.t: The cat watched from the road.
s.fr: Le chat observait depuis la route.

s.t: The coach rode on.
s.fr: Le carrosse continua sa route.

s.t: The cat had more to do.
s.fr: Le chat avait encore plus à faire.

s.t: He ran ahead of the coach.
s.fr: Il courut en avant du carrosse.

s.t: He wanted to reach the fields.
s.fr: Il voulait atteindre les champs.

paras.summary: The cat watches from the road as the coach rides on, but the cat still has more to do, so he runs ahead of the coach, wanting to reach the fields, for only the cat knows what comes next.

s.t: Soon the cat came to a field.
s.fr: Bientôt le chat arriva à un champ.

s.t: Harvesters were cutting grain in the field.
s.fr: Des moissonneurs coupaient du grain dans le champ.

s.t: The fields belonged to a rich ogre.
s.fr: Les champs appartenaient à un riche ogre.

s.t: No harvester had ever seen the ogre.
s.fr: Aucun moissonneur n’avait jamais vu l’ogre.

s.t: The cat ran to the harvesters.
s.fr: Le chat courut vers les moissonneurs.

paras.summary: Soon the cat comes to a field where harvesters are cutting grain; the fields belong to a rich ogre that no harvester has ever seen, but the cat still wants to help the son, so he runs to the harvesters.

s.t: "The king will soon ride by," the cat said.
s.fr: « Le roi passera bientôt par ici, » dit le chat.

s.t: "You will say this field belongs to the Marquis of Carabas."
s.fr: « Vous direz que ce champ appartient au Marquis de Carabas. »

s.t: "If not, I will cut you into pieces," said the cat.
s.fr: « Sinon, je vous couperai en morceaux, » dit le chat.

s.t: The harvesters were afraid of the cat.
s.fr: Les moissonneurs avaient peur du chat.

s.t: They believed every word.
s.fr: Ils crurent chaque mot.

s.t: They said they would always do it.
s.fr: Ils dirent qu’ils le feraient toujours.

s.t: The cat ran on ahead of the coach.
s.fr: Le chat courut en avant du carrosse.

paras.summary: "You will say this field belongs to the Marquis of Carabas, or I will cut you into pieces," says the cat, and the afraid harvesters believe every word and say they will do it, so the cat runs on ahead of the coach.

s.t: The coach came to the field.
s.fr: Le carrosse arriva au champ.

s.t: "Whose field is this?" the king asked.
s.fr: « À qui appartient ce champ ? » demanda le roi.

s.t: "This field belongs to the Marquis of Carabas," the harvesters said.
s.fr: « Ce champ appartient au Marquis de Carabas, » dirent les moissonneurs.

s.t: The king was surprised.
s.fr: Le roi fut surpris.

s.t: He would remember this rich Marquis.
s.fr: Il se souviendrait de ce riche Marquis.

paras.summary: The coach comes to the field, and when the king asks whose field it is, the harvesters, still afraid, say it belongs to the Marquis of Carabas; the surprised king would remember this rich Marquis.

s.t: "The Marquis has so much land," the king said to the princess.
s.fr: « Le Marquis possède tant de terres, » dit le roi à la princesse.

s.t: The princess wanted to meet the Marquis.
s.fr: La princesse voulait rencontrer le Marquis.

s.t: The coach rode on.
s.fr: Le carrosse continua sa route.

s.t: Soon they left the fields.
s.fr: Bientôt ils quittèrent les champs.

s.t: The cat was already far ahead.
s.fr: Le chat était déjà loin devant.

s.t: He had one more place to reach.
s.fr: Il avait encore un endroit à atteindre.

paras.summary: "The Marquis has so much land," the king tells the princess, who wants to meet the Marquis and is happy to hear this, and the coach rides on until they leave the fields, but the cat is already far ahead, with one more place left to reach.

s.t: Soon the cat reached a great castle.
s.fr: Bientôt le chat atteignit un grand château.

s.t: The castle was near the fields.
s.fr: Le château était près de les champs.

s.t: The ogre was the richest in the land.
s.fr: L’ogre était le plus riche du pays.

s.t: The ogre owned three castles like this one.
s.fr: L’ogre possédait trois châteaux comme celui-ci.

s.t: A servant brought the cat inside.
s.fr: Un serviteur amena le chat à l’intérieur.

paras.summary: Soon the cat reaches a great castle near the fields, the ogre's home; the ogre is the richest in the land and owns three castles like this one, and the king's coach will soon come here too, so a servant brings the cat inside.

s.t: The cat was not afraid to ask.
s.fr: Le chat n’avait pas peur de demander.

s.t: "I want to see the great ogre," said the cat.
s.fr: « Je veux voir le grand ogre, » dit-il le chat.

s.t: The servant brought the cat to the ogre.
s.fr: Le serviteur amena le chat à l’ogre.

s.t: The ogre was strong and proud.
s.fr: L’ogre était fort et fier.

paras.summary: The cat is not afraid to ask for the ogre, and the servant brings the cat to him; the ogre is strong and proud.

s.t: The ogre always liked to talk.
s.fr: L’ogre aimait toujours parler.

s.t: "I heard you can change into any animal," the cat said.
s.fr: « J’ai entendu que vous pouvez vous transformer en n’importe quel animal, » dit le chat.

s.t: "Is this true?" the cat asked.
s.fr: « Est-ce vrai ? » demanda le chat.

paras.summary: The ogre always likes to talk, and the cat, with a clever plan for him, says he heard the ogre can change into any animal and asks if this is true.

s.t: "This is true," said the ogre.
s.fr: « C’est vrai, » dit l’ogre.

s.t: The cat had seen many rich castles.
s.fr: Le chat avait vu beaucoup de châteaux riches.

s.t: The ogre became a big lion.
s.fr: L’ogre devint un grand lion.

s.t: The lion roared.
s.fr: Le lion rugit.

paras.summary: "This is true," says the ogre; this magic is new to the cat, who has seen many rich castles but never this, and the ogre becomes a big lion that roars, a roar that everyone in the castle hears.

s.t: The cat was afraid of the lion.
s.fr: Le chat avait peur du lion.

s.t: The cat did not want to become dinner.
s.fr: Le chat ne voulait pas devenir le dîner.

s.t: The cat ran up to the roof.
s.fr: Le chat courut jusqu’au toit.

paras.summary: The cat is afraid of the lion and does not want to become dinner, but he still believes in his own plan, so he runs up to the roof.

s.t: His boots made it hard to climb.
s.fr: Ses bottes rendaient la montée difficile.

s.t: But the cat still held on.
s.fr: Mais le chat tenait encore bon.

s.t: The lion looked up at the cat.
s.fr: Le lion regarda le chat en haut.

s.t: Soon the lion became the ogre.
s.fr: Bientôt le lion devint l’ogre.

s.t: The ogre laughed at the afraid cat.
s.fr: L’ogre rit du chat apeuré.

paras.summary: His boots make it hard to climb, but the cat still holds on while the lion looks up at him; soon the lion becomes the ogre, who laughs at the afraid cat.

s.t: Soon the cat came down from the roof.
s.fr: Bientôt le chat descendit du toit.

s.t: "That was a great trick," said the cat.
s.fr: « C’était un grand tour », dit-il le chat.

s.t: "But I do not believe you can become small," the cat said.
s.fr: « Mais je ne crois pas que vous puissiez devenir petit, » dit-il le chat.

s.t: "Small like a mouse," the cat said.
s.fr: « Petit comme une souris, » dit le chat.

s.t: The proud ogre wanted to prove this.
s.fr: L’ogre fier voulut prouver cela.

paras.summary: Soon the cat comes down from the roof, still afraid of the ogre, and says that was a great trick, but he does not believe the ogre can become small, like a mouse, so the proud ogre wants to prove this.

s.t: The ogre became a small mouse.
s.fr: L’ogre devint une petite souris.

s.t: The mouse ran across the floor.
s.fr: La souris courut à travers le sol.

s.t: The cat jumped on the mouse.
s.fr: Le chat sauta sur la souris.

s.t: The cat ate the mouse.
s.fr: Le chat mangea la souris.

s.t: The ogre was dead.
s.fr: L’ogre était mort.

s.t: Now the castle belonged to no one.
s.fr: Maintenant le château n’appartenait à personne.

paras.summary: The ogre becomes a small mouse that runs across the floor, but the cat jumps on the mouse and eats it, so the ogre is dead, and now the castle belongs to no one, though the son will soon own this rich castle.

s.t: Soon the king's coach reached the castle.
s.fr: Bientôt le carrosse du roi atteignit le château.

s.t: The young man was still with them.
s.fr: Le jeune homme était encore avec eux.

s.t: The cat stood at the castle gate.
s.fr: Le chat se tenait à la porte du château.

s.t: "Welcome to my master's castle," said the cat.
s.fr: « Bienvenue dans le château de mon maître, » dit le chat.

s.t: "This is the castle of the Marquis of Carabas," the cat said.
s.fr: « C’est le château du Marquis de Carabas, » dit le chat.

s.t: The king was surprised by the great castle.
s.fr: Le roi fut surpris par le grand château.

s.t: They all went inside.
s.fr: Ils entrèrent tous à l’intérieur.

paras.summary: Soon the king's coach reaches the castle with the young man still with them, and the cat, standing at the castle gate, welcomes them to his master's castle, the castle of the Marquis of Carabas, so the king, surprised by the great castle, goes inside with the rest.

s.t: The servants had made a great feast.
s.fr: Les serviteurs avaient préparé un grand festin.

s.t: This feast was for the ogre's friends.
s.fr: Ce festin était pour les amis de l’ogre.

s.t: The princess and the king ate the feast.
s.fr: La princesse et le roi mangèrent le festin.

s.t: The king liked the rich castle so much.
s.fr: Le roi aimait beaucoup le riche château.

s.t: The king wanted the Marquis for his daughter.
s.fr: Le roi voulait le Marquis pour sa fille.

paras.summary: The servants had made a great feast for the ogre's friends, but the ogre is dead now, so the king and the princess eat the feast; the king likes the rich castle so much that he wants the Marquis for his daughter.

s.t: The king gave his daughter to the Marquis.
s.fr: Le roi donna sa fille au Marquis.

s.t: Soon the Marquis married the princess.
s.fr: Bientôt le Marquis épousa la princesse.

s.t: The wedding was at the castle.
s.fr: Le mariage eut lieu au château.

s.t: The son was now a real marquis.
s.fr: Le fils était maintenant un vrai marquis.

paras.summary: The king gives his daughter to the Marquis, and soon the Marquis marries the princess in a wedding at the castle, for the son is now a real marquis.

s.t: The son once had only the cat.
s.fr: Le fils n’avait eu autrefois que le chat.

s.t: The Marquis always remembered the clever cat.
s.fr: Le Marquis se souvenait toujours du chat intelligent.

s.t: The cat lived with them in the castle.
s.fr: Le chat vivait avec eux dans le château.

s.t: He became a great lord too.
s.fr: Il devint aussi un grand seigneur.

s.t: The cat did not need to catch a mouse now.
s.fr: Le chat n’avait plus besoin d’attraper une souris maintenant.

s.t: But the cat still liked to catch one.
s.fr: Mais le chat aimait encore en attraper une.

paras.summary: The son once had only the cat, and the Marquis always remembers the clever cat, who lives with them in the castle and becomes a great lord too; the cat does not need to catch a mouse now, but he still likes to catch one.
